title.en: I Cannot Remember My Mother: a poem by Rabindranath Tagore

text.en: You may forget a face but still recognise a song or a smell from long ago. In this poem a child who cannot remember his mother still finds her everywhere.

I Cannot Remember My Mother is a poem by Rabindranath Tagore in which the speaker says he has no clear memory of his mother.
Each of the three stanzas begins with the same line, which is a refrain. It stresses the sadness of not remembering.
In the first stanza a tune seems to hover over his playthings, the tune of a song she hummed while rocking his cradle. This is auditory imagery.
In the second stanza the smell of shiuli flowers on an autumn morning brings the scent of the temple's morning service, and he feels it as the scent of his mother. This is olfactory imagery, about smell.
In the third stanza, looking into the blue distance from his window, he feels his mother's gaze has spread all over the sky. This is visual imagery and a metaphor that makes the sky a comforting presence.
So the three stanzas move through three senses: hearing, smell and sight. The mother is felt in ordinary moments of play, morning and sky.
The poem is written in free verse, without a regular rhyme scheme, in simple conversational language.
The mood is tender and longing, and the theme is that love lives on in everyday things even when direct memory is lost.

problem.en: Match each stanza with the sense it uses.

text.en: Stanza 1 uses the tune he hears while playing.
Stanza 2 uses the smell of shiuli flowers.
Stanza 3 uses the blue sky and her gaze.

prompt.en: How does the poet show his mother's presence although he cannot remember her?

requiredIdeas.en: Tune, scent and sky bring her back

points.en: The poem by Rabindranath Tagore is about a child who cannot remember his mother but feels her presence.
The refrain opens each of the three stanzas.
It uses hearing, smell and sight imagery.
The mood is tender and longing.
